purpose: Select a memory-safe ordinary-proof-term import for all 66 frozen LRAT refutations.

mathematical_scope.acceptance: Each segment is reconstructed by Mathlib's proof-producing LRAT step builder; the last declaration has type Sat.Fmla.proof formula [].
mathematical_scope.coverage_check: For every case, the concatenation of the binary segment files must be byte-for-byte identical to the frozen source LRAT binary.

calibrations.observation: The largest direct and cube-leaf imports retained 14-22 GiB and continued growing; the route was not safe at full scale.
The 3.45 MB text trace remained unfinished after 750 seconds, making the 96 MB hard trace impractical despite a roughly 2.1 GiB working set.
Named checkpoints in one module still retained prior declaration values; working memory reached 17.0 GiB after about 60 seconds.
All 15 modules built successfully and the final theorem depended only on propext. Binary slices totaled exactly 1,657,867 bytes, matching the source binary.

calibrations.variant: one Lean module per at most 1,000,000 text bytes and 10,000 additions
calibrations.observation: This retains exact binary coverage, bounds measured memory, reduces the full campaign to 572 proof segments, and keeps all certificate source below the Palomar repository-size limit.

full_campaign_projection.parallelism_policy: Use at most four independent case chains concurrently and keep whole-machine physical-memory use below 54 GiB.

verification.negative_fixture: Malformed or missing clause identifiers are rejected by buildProofStep and checkpoint cardinality checks.
verification.translation_check: Every manifest records both the frozen source-binary hash and the concatenated segment hash; generation aborts unless they agree exactly.
verification.kernel_fixture: All 66 final refutations compiled in the clean four-lane build, and every #print axioms report was exactly [propext].
